# Results — Study 602 (Macro-Announcement-Day Premium)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test
(Savor & Wilson 2013) — **most of the equity premium is earned on scheduled macro-announcement
days** (CPI releases, Employment Situation "NFP" releases, FOMC decision days) — rebuilt on SPY
(+ TLT) daily total-return closes against a hardcoded, source-documented release calendar,
1997 → 2026. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete month; the partial current month is
dropped). Fingerprint `e42015f7ee3e`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes — SPY (7,419 daily returns, 1997-01-02 → 2026-06-30, **29.5 years**) + TLT (6,016 daily returns, 2002-08 →) |
| Calendar | hardcoded in [`data.py`](../macro_announcement_premium/data.py): **236 FOMC** scheduled decision days (Fed historical calendars) + **353 CPI** + **353 NFP** actual release days (BLS archive index `bls.gov/bls/news-release/{cpi,empsit}.htm` cross-checked against the official `histreleasedates.pdf` — 19/19 overlapping 1999-2000 dates agree) |
| A-days | **923 distinct announcement sessions** = **12.4%** of all sessions; 19 sessions carry 2 announcement types; 10 holiday releases mapped to the next session |
| Survivorship | SPY/TLT are broad index ETFs — **survivorship-clean** at the vehicle level |
| Execution / costs | the release schedule is published in advance → enter the **prior session's close**, exit the A-day close (one execution lag, one round trip per A-day); **1 / 2 / 5 bps** one-way × NAV; long-only, no borrow; raw total-return (no T-bill credit on idle cash — a conservative omission that penalises the overlay) |

### Calendar spot-checks (construction sanity)

- NFP releases fall on **Friday 96.0%** of the time; all 14 in-window non-Fridays are documented
  exceptions (July-4th-week Thursdays, the 1998-11-05 early release, shutdown-delayed reports
  2013-10-22 / 2025-11-20 / 2025-12-16, 2026-02-11 schedule slip).
- CPI day-of-month spans **10 → 30** (mid-month schedule; >15th = shutdown-delayed releases,
  e.g. 2013-10-30 and 2025-10-24; the Oct-2025 CPI was never published — 2025 has 11 releases).
- **0** weekend release dates (must be 0). One archive-filename quirk corrected
  (`empsit_01192000.txt` → official release date 2000-01-07 per `histreleasedates.pdf`).

## Headline — announcement days vs all other days (SPY close-to-close, total-return)

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| A-day mean | **+10.63 bps/day** (n = 923; one-sample *t*₀ = 2.55) |
| other-day mean | +3.69 bps/day (n = 6,496) |
| **pooled premium (A − rest)** | **+6.94 bps/day**  ·  Welch *t* = **+1.57** |
| share of cumulative return | **12.4%** of sessions carry **32.1%** of SPY's cumulative log return |
| placebo *p* (20,000 random same-density calendars) | **0.0563** |

The pooled announcement-day premium is **positive but does not clear the desk's t ≥ 2 bar**:
Welch *t* = 1.57, placebo *p* = 0.056. A-days do carry an outsized share of the return (2.6×
their day share), but on this 29.5-year tape the pooled CPI+NFP+FOMC claim cannot be certified —
**WEAK**, per the inference bar ("the literature says real; this tape alone can't certify it").

## Per-type split — each type vs pure non-announcement days

| type | n | A-day mean (bps) | diff vs rest (bps) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **FOMC** | 236 | +22.20 | **+18.52** | **+2.25** |
| CPI | 353 | +4.55 | +0.87 | +0.12 |
| NFP | 353 | +13.24 | +9.56 | +1.38 |

Only the **FOMC leg** clears *t* ≥ 2. CPI days are indistinguishable from ordinary days; NFP
days lean positive but do not clear.

## Sub-periods (decades, pooled A-days)

| window | A-mean (bps) | rest (bps) | diff (bps) | Welch *t* | n A-days |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1997-2006 | +13.92 | +2.46 | +11.46 | +1.51 | 315 |
| 2007-2016 | +14.05 | +2.01 | +12.04 | +1.56 | 312 |
| 2017-2026 | +3.53 | +6.75 | **−3.22** | −0.42 | 296 |

The premium lived in 1997-2016 and has been **absent (slightly negative) since 2017**.

## TLT (long Treasuries) — same calendar, 2002-08 →

A-day mean **−0.56** vs other-day **+2.18** bps/day; diff **−2.74** bps/day, Welch *t* =
**−0.68** (n_A = 749, 6,016 days). Savor-Wilson's Treasury-side announcement premium does
**not** show on the TLT window — no announcement-day premium in long bonds here.

## Tradable overlay — long SPY only on announcement days

One round trip per A-day (31.4/yr), 12.4% time in market, enter prior close / exit A-day close.

| one-way cost | gross (bps/A-day) | net (bps/A-day) | net *t*₀ | net ann | buy & hold ann |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 bps | +10.63 | +8.63 | **+2.07** | **+2.48%** | +10.05% |
| 2 bps | +10.63 | +6.63 | +1.59 | +1.84% | +10.05% |
| 5 bps | +10.63 | +0.63 | +0.15 | **−0.05%** | +10.05% |

Even at an institutional 1 bp/leg the overlay nets only **+2.48%/yr vs +10.05%** for simply
holding SPY — it throws away three-quarters of the market return to time the calendar — and at
a realistic 5 bps it is **dead** (net −0.05%/yr). The net edge is not deployable: **MIRAGE**.
*(No T-bill credit on the 87.6% cash days is modeled; adding it would still leave the overlay
far under buy & hold at retail costs and does not change the stamp.)*

## Third axis — is it all just FOMC?

The pooled Savor-Wilson framing sells CPI and NFP as premium carriers alongside FOMC. Remove
the FOMC sessions and test what is left:

| leg | n | diff vs pure non-A (bps/day) | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **CPI/NFP-only A-days (no FOMC)** | 687 | +2.97 | **+0.58** | 0.3175 |
| FOMC decision days | 236 | +18.52 | **+2.25** | — |

FOMC-only engine by decade (vs all other days in the same decade): 1997-2006 **+14.28** bps/day
(*t* = 1.21) · 2007-2016 **+45.29** (*t* = **2.90**) · 2017-2026 **−6.09** (*t* = −0.41).

**CONFIRMED — it is all FOMC.** The CPI/NFP legs contribute a statistical zero (+2.97 bps/day,
*t* = 0.58, placebo *p* = 0.32); the entire pooled premium is carried by the 236 FOMC decision
days (*t* = 2.25) — and even that engine is concentrated in 2007-2016 (*t* = 2.90) and has been
absent since 2017 (*t* = −0.41), consistent with the desk's FOMC-drift teardowns
([517](../517-pre-fomc-drift/), [67](../67-fed-drift/), [135](../135-fomc-cycle/)).

## Synthetic control — the engine is faithful (100 seeds, machinery proof only)

| planted edge | mean diff (bps/day) | mean Welch *t* | share \|t\| ≥ 2 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **0 bps** (null) | +0.45 | **+0.10** | 4% |
| **+20 bps** | +20.45 | **+4.72** | 100% |

With no planted premium the A-vs-rest detector sits at *t* ≈ 0.1 and a ~4% false-positive rate
(nominal); a +20 bps/day planted premium is recovered at mean *t* = 4.7 in 100/100 seeds. The
machinery is unbiased and well-powered — so the real-tape *t* = 1.57 is a genuine sub-bar
reading, not a power failure. *(Never cited in support of a stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The pooled macro-announcement-day premium is **+6.94 bps/day** but only
  **Welch *t* = 1.57** (placebo *p* = 0.056) on 29.5 years of SPY — below the desk's **t ≥ 2**
  bar. The only leg that clears is **FOMC** (*t* = 2.25); CPI and NFP days carry nothing
  (*t* = 0.12 / 1.38), and the pooled effect has been **absent since 2017** (diff −3.22
  bps/day). The literature says real (1958-2009); this tape alone can't certify the pooled
  claim. WEAK, not REAL — and not NONE, because A-days still carry 32% of the return on 12% of
  the days and the FOMC leg is genuine.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The A-day-only overlay nets **+2.48%/yr at 1 bp vs +10.05%** buy &
  hold, and is **negative at 5 bps** (31.4 round trips/yr). You give up most of the equity
  return to harvest a premium that costs eat — nothing deployable survives.
- **"Is it all just FOMC?" — CONFIRMED.** Ex-FOMC announcement days earn **+2.97 bps/day over
  ordinary days (*t* = 0.58, placebo *p* = 0.32)** — a statistical zero. The pooled
  "macro-announcement premium" is, on this tape, the **FOMC-day premium wearing a bigger
  calendar**, and even that engine faded after 2017.
